S8.01.needs: a password recovery link (or a way to open the reset-password route)
S8.01.note: The screen is reached by a deep link (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx routes segments reset-password), so there is no in-app menu path; the primary style itself is the default variant in apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx (teal fill).
steps: Open the password recovery link so the Reset password screen opens (the app routes to (auth)/reset-password).
Read the text: "Password recovery opens in your AGI web account."
Look at the filled teal button "Open Web Account" (default primary style).
Compare the label colour with the button fill: it should be readable.
Compare with Expected: the main action has the emphasised primary style.
S8.01.where: Reset password screen (opened from a password recovery link, not from a menu) > Open Web Account button

labels.text: Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device?

S8.02.note: The outline style is set by variant="outline" in apps/mobile/app/(auth)/reset-password.tsx; the outline colours are in apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx.
steps: Open the Reset password screen (same route as S8.01).
Look at the buttons under the text: "Open Web Account" is filled, "Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device?" and "Back to Sign In" have an outline style.
Compare the outline buttons with the filled one: they should look less prominent.
Check that the outline buttons sit beside the primary action.
S8.02.where: Reset password screen > Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device? button

S8.03.needs: a paid account with at least one scheduled task (Scheduled tasks need Basic)
S8.03.note: The destructive style is variant="destructive" in apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx (text colour agentError); other destructive buttons also exist, e.g. apps/mobile/src/features/sites/SiteDetailScreen.tsx.
steps: Open an existing scheduled task (the Schedules screen is opened from "Create schedule" or the schedule list; how Schedules is opened from the main menu was not traced).
Open the edit form of that schedule.
Scroll to the bottom and find the red "Delete Schedule" button.
Look at the label colour (danger colour) and check it is readable.
Compare with Expected: the irreversible action uses the distinct destructive style.
S8.03.where: Schedule form for an existing schedule > Delete Schedule button

S8.04.needs: a chat with messages; a phone-width layout (not the wide persistent drawer)
S8.04.note: The button is not shown when the wide persistent drawer is used (usesPersistentDrawer), so a Mac window that is wide may show a different header.
steps: Open any chat from the chat list.
Find the icon-only button at the top left of the chat header (a menu icon, no words).
Tap it: the side drawer should open.
Check that the button has an accessible name "Open menu" (for example with VoiceOver, if the tester uses it).
Compare with Expected: the icon-only button has an accessible name.
S8.04.where: Chat screen (phone width) > Open menu icon at the top left of the chat header

S8.06.needs: a phone with a back camera and a torch; camera permission (not possible on a Mac without a camera)
S8.06.note: The torch label "Turn torch on" / "Turn torch off" is in apps/mobile/app/(app)/camera.tsx and the selected state is set with accessibilityState; a Mac tester may not be able to run it.
steps: Open a chat and tap the "Add to chat" button next to the message box.
Tap "Camera" in the sheet and allow camera access.
On the camera screen, tap the torch button (only shown on the back camera); its label is "Turn torch on".
Tap it again: the label should change to "Turn torch off" and the torch should toggle.
Compare with Expected: a button that shows an on or off pressed state.
S8.06.where: Add to chat (plus button under the composer) > Camera > camera screen > torch icon at the bottom

labels.text: Sent to the agent with Allow or Deny

S8.07.needs: a cloud account and a request that needs tool approval
S8.07.note: Known unfinished: the approve and deny row is not exposed as a labelled button group. The visible words Allow and Deny come from TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS, whose source file was not found; the label text is only visible in the code as a hint.
steps: Start a cloud chat whose agent asks to use a tool (the tool approval card appears).
Look at the row of buttons for the decision (Allow and Deny).
Check whether the row is announced as one labelled group (it is not, per the code).
Compare with Expected: related buttons are grouped under one label.
S8.07.where: Chat reply that asks for tool approval > Allow / Deny buttons under the request

S8.08.needs: a cloud or local chat that returns links
S8.08.note: MessageContentRenderer.tsx is the renderer for message text, but no link-open call was found in it; the opening behaviour may live in another file, so it was not verified.
steps: Open a chat and ask for an answer that includes a web address or link (for example, a question that needs sources).
Look at the reply: links should be styled as links (coloured text).
Tap a link and check that its destination opens.
Compare with Expected: the link is styled as a link and opens its destination.
S8.08.where: Chat > ask a question whose answer contains a web link > tap the link in the reply

S8.09.needs: none for the Projects search; the Personalization field needs a signed-in account
S8.09.note: The Personalization row is labelled "Personalization" in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx (the Settings screen entry from the menu was not traced).
steps: Tap the Projects tab at the bottom.
Tap the search field with the text "Search projects" and type a word.
Check the list filters as you type, and that the field has a clear button.
Alternatively open Personalization and tap the "Full Name" field, then type a name.
Compare with Expected: a single-line field with a visible label or accessible name.
S8.09.where: Projects tab > Search projects field; or Settings > Personalization > Full Name field

S8.10.needs: none; the placeholder may differ when offline
S8.10.note: The composer's accessible name is "Message input" (ChatInput.tsx); the placeholder depends on state (line 1657), so the exact visible word may change.
steps: Open the Chat tab and tap the message box at the bottom.
Type one line, then press the Return key on the keyboard.
Check that the cursor moves to a new line inside the same box and the text is not sent.
Compare with Expected: a multi-line text area that accepts new lines is used.
S8.10.where: Chat tab > message box at the bottom (placeholder "Type or hold to talk")

S8.11.note: The search screen is apps/mobile/app/(app)/search.tsx, which renders ChatsListScreen; the drawer search icon's route was inferred and not traced.
steps: Open the side drawer from the menu icon at the top left of the chat screen.
Tap the search icon in the drawer (its word is a translation key "search"; no visible word was found).
Type text in the field with placeholder "Search".
Check that the list of chats, projects, files and artifacts filters as you type.
Compare with Expected: a search field that filters the list.
S8.11.where: Search icon in the drawer (opened from the Open menu icon) > Search field with placeholder "Search"

S8.12.note: The field is secureTextEntry in AddCustomConnectorModal.tsx; the Settings screen entry from the menu was not traced.
steps: Open Connectors from the Settings screen.
Tap "Add custom MCP".
In the modal, tap the "Auth token (optional)" field and type a few characters.
Check that the characters show as dots (masked), not plain text.
Compare with Expected: secret entry uses a masked field.
S8.12.where: Connectors > Add custom MCP > Auth token (optional) field

S8.13.needs: an email inbox you can read (the code is sent by an outside email service)
S8.13.note: The code field uses textContentType oneTimeCode in MobileSignIn.tsx; whether the "Use an email code instead" link is always shown was not fully traced.
steps: On the sign-in screen, tap "Email address" and type your email.
Tap "Continue".
Tap "Use an email code instead" if it is shown.
Look for the field labelled "Verification code" with the text "Enter the code sent to" and your email.
Type the code from your email (or paste it) and check that it accepts a one-time code.
S8.13.where: Sign-in screen > type email > Continue > Use an email code instead > Verification code field

S8.14.note: The day toggles use accessibilityRole checkbox in TimeFocusScreen.tsx; how the Notifications screen is opened from the main menu was not traced.
steps: Open Notifications from Settings and tap "Quiet hours".
Open the time and focus screen and find the "Days" row with one letter per day.
Tap a day letter and check that it toggles on or off.
Check the day shows as checked (selected).
Compare with Expected: independent on or off choices with checked state.
S8.14.where: Settings > Notifications > Quiet hours > Days row (Sunday to Saturday)

S8.15.note: The style row in AddToChatSheet.tsx calls onOpenStyleSelector, but its visible text was not found; the options use accessibilityRole radio.
steps: Open a chat and tap the "Add to chat" button.
Find the style entry in the sheet and tap it (its visible label was not found in the code).
In the style list, tap "Concise" and check that the selected row is marked selected.
Tap "Formal" and check that the selection moves.
Compare with Expected: one choice at a time, all options visible, with checked state.
S8.15.where: Chat > Add to chat > style row (opens the style selector) > Normal, Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal

S8.16.needs: a device with calendar access (the switch asks for permission)
S8.16.note: The calendar switch is in apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/integrations.tsx; the Settings entry from the main menu was not traced.
steps: Open Device Integrations from Settings.
Find the calendar row with a switch on its right.
Tap the switch and check it turns on or off immediately.
Compare with Expected: an immediate on or off setting with switch semantics.
S8.16.where: Settings > Device Integrations > calendar row switch

S8.17.needs: a Cloud-enabled account to change to Cloud (Cloud is disabled otherwise)
S8.17.note: The control is labelled "Chat execution mode" (tablist) and is also in Settings (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx).
steps: Open the side drawer from the menu icon.
Find the two-part control with the segments "Local" and "Cloud".
Tap "Local" and check it is highlighted; tap "Cloud" and check the highlight moves.
Compare with Expected: a small set of exclusive options shown as joined segments.
S8.17.where: Open menu (top left of a chat) > drawer > Local | Cloud segmented control

S8.18.needs: none; some models need a paid plan
S8.18.note: The Choose a model control appears in the retired-model notice in the chat; the model list is ModelPickerSheet and the Settings screen entry was not traced.
steps: Open the Models row from Settings (the row is labelled "Models").
Tap a model in the list.
Check the chosen model is marked selected and the row value updates.
Compare with Expected: one value chosen from a list.
S8.18.where: Settings > Models (row shows the current model) > model list; or the Choose a model control in the chat

S8.19.note: The search field has accessibilityLabel "Search models" and a listbox-like list; keyboard arrow navigation was not verified.
steps: Open the model picker (Models row or Choose a model).
Tap the field with the placeholder "Search models…" and type part of a model name.
Check the list filters as you type.
Tap a result and check it is chosen.
Compare with Expected: type to filter, then pick one.
S8.19.where: Settings > Models, or Choose a model > search field "Search models…"

S8.23.note: The slider is VoiceSlider in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice/index.tsx, not the personalization file cited in the plan, which has no slider.
steps: Open Voice from Settings.
Find the row labelled "Speed" with a value such as 1.00x.
Drag the slider or tap near its ends, and check the value changes in steps.
Compare with Expected: one value set on a scale by dragging.

S8.25.needs: a paid account that allows scheduled tasks (Basic or higher)
S8.25.note: On iOS the calendar is inline; on other platforms the native picker is used, per ScheduleDateTimeField.tsx.
steps: Open the schedules screen and tap the "Create schedule" button.
Choose the once recurrence option (its word was not found in the code).
Tap the "Date" field showing "Choose a date".
Pick a date on the calendar and check the field shows that date.
Compare with Expected: a date picker is used where a date is entered.
S8.25.where: Schedules > Create schedule > Repeat set to once > Date field "Choose a date"

S8.26.needs: a paid account that allows scheduled tasks
S8.26.note: The spinner display is used only on iOS (Platform.OS === 'ios' in ScheduleDateTimeField.tsx); the recurrence word that shows the time was not traced.
steps: Open "Create schedule" and choose a recurrence that shows a time (the time row appears for supported recurrences).
Tap the "Preferred time" field showing "Choose a time" or its value (default 09:00).
Change the time in the spinner and tap done if shown.
Check the field shows the new time.
Compare with Expected: a time control is used where a time is entered.
S8.26.where: Schedules > Create schedule > recurrence with a time > "Preferred time" field "Choose a time"

S8.27.needs: a paid account that allows scheduled tasks
S8.27.note: The row's accessibility label is "Time zone: <zone>"; the default device zone comes from getDeviceTimezone() in ScheduleForm.tsx.
steps: Open "Create schedule" and scroll to the zone row labelled with "Time zone:" and the zone name.
Tap the row to open the time zone list.
Type part of a zone name in the "Search time zones" field.
Check the list filters, and that the device zone is the default.
Compare with Expected: a searchable list of zones, defaulting to the device zone.
S8.27.where: Schedules > Create schedule > Time zone row (shows the current zone) > search field "Search time zones"

S8.28.note: The swatches are in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/accent-color/index.tsx; the swatch labels are in that file's ACCENTS list.
steps: Open Settings and tap "Accent Color".
Tap a swatch such as "Blue" and check the swatch is selected.
Check the accent colour changes in the app (for example, buttons turn blue).
Compare with Expected: a colour choice from swatches.
S8.28.where: Settings > Accent Color > colour swatches (Neutral, Blue, Cyan, Green, Lime)

S8.29.needs: a file to upload on the device
S8.29.note: The picker is DocumentPicker.getDocumentAsync in apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx; mobile file types depend on the execution mode.
steps: Open a chat and tap the "Add to chat" button.
Tap "File" in the sheet.
Pick a file from the device document picker and confirm.
Check that the file appears as an attachment above the message box.
Compare with Expected: a file input chooses files from the device.

S8.31.needs: a project (create one first if none exists)
S8.31.note: Tabs use accessibilityRole tab with accessibilityState selected; the visible name of the Projects bottom tab was not found exactly, and "Work" appears only when showWork is true.
steps: Tap the Projects tab at the bottom and open any project.
Look at the row of tabs at the top of the project.
Tap "Sources" and check its panel appears and its tab is marked selected.
Tap "Artifacts" and then "Routines", checking each panel changes.
Compare with Expected: a tab row that switches panels, with the selected tab marked.
S8.31.where: Projects tab > open a project > tabs "Chats", "Sources", "Artifacts", "Routines" ("Work" when shown)

S8.32.needs: a signed-in account that can send chat messages that use tools
S8.32.note: The row's accessible name is built as Show or Hide plus the summary, and it only appears when the reply has tool activity.
steps: Tap Open menu, then tap the new-chat button in the chat header (New chat).
Send a question that needs a tool, such as a web search.
Find the Agent activity row under the assistant reply.
Tap the row; it should expand to show the activity and collapse on a second tap.
Compare with Expected: the row's expanded state changes on each tap and the header is labelled as a button.
S8.32.where: Open menu > New chat > send a message that makes the assistant use a tool (for example a web search) > tap the Agent activity row under the reply

S8.33.needs: a signed-in account and a question that returns web sources
S8.33.note: The number in the row is filled in from the source count, for example View 3 sources.
steps: Tap Open menu, then the new-chat button (New chat).
Ask a question that returns web sources.
Under the reply, tap the View N sources row (N is the number of sources).
Look for the expanded list titled Sources (or Sources so far while the answer is still streaming).
Compare with Expected: the block shows and hides, and the expanded state changes on each tap.
S8.33.where: Open menu > New chat > ask a question that returns web sources > tap View N sources under the reply

S8.34.needs: a microphone and a device that supports switching the audio route
S8.34.note: The picker returns nothing on platforms without audio route switching, so it may not appear on a given device.
steps: Open Settings and tap Voice.
Start a voice call from the voice screen (the start control was not confirmed in the code).
In the live voice bar, tap the audio route button, labelled Audio route followed by the current route.
See whether a list of routes opens (Automatic, Speaker, Bluetooth, Headset) and choose one.
Compare with Expected: the list opens, and the button label changes to the chosen route.
S8.34.where: Settings > Voice > open the voice call screen > tap the audio route button in the live voice bar (Audio route, Automatic)

S8.35.note: Archive appears only for AGI Cloud chats, and some items depend on the chat's state.
steps: Tap Open menu to open the side list of chats.
Long-press a chat title.
Look for the action menu that opens for that chat, listing actions such as Rename.
Compare with Expected: the menu opens for the chat you pressed and lists its actions; tapping outside closes it.
S8.35.where: Open menu > long-press a chat in the list > choose from the menu (Rename, Archive, Delete and others)

S8.40.needs: a notification with High or Critical priority (not every account has one)
S8.40.note: The shared badge component is apps/mobile/components/ui/Badge.tsx; the notifications link may not show in the menu on every build, so confirm it on screen.
steps: Tap Open menu.
Tap the notifications link (its accessible name reads Open notifications with the unread count).
Look at the small tag on each notification row, such as High or Critical.
Compare with Expected: each notification shows a small status or priority marker attached to it.
Also open Agents, tap an agent, and look for the status badge at the top of the agent screen.
S8.40.where: Open menu > Notifications, then look at the priority tag on each notification

S8.41.needs: at least one artifact in the account
S8.41.note: No user-editable tag control was found; the only label on a card is the computed kind or language, so the word varies per artifact.
steps: Tap Search (the search icon in the side menu).
Type Artifacts and tap the Artifacts result under Go to.
Look at the small label on each non-image artifact card; it shows the artifact's language or kind.
Compare with Expected: the label names what the item is; it is a type label, not a free tag the user adds.
S8.41.where: Search > type Artifacts > tap Artifacts > look at the small label on each artifact card

S8.42.needs: a signed-in account that can get a reply
S8.42.note: No picture avatar was found; the author marker is a text name in the message's accessible label, and the visible name rendering was not confirmed in code.
steps: Tap Open menu, then the new-chat button (New chat).
Send any message and wait for the reply.
Look at who wrote each message: your message is marked You, the reply uses the model name or AGI.
Compare with Expected: the two authors are told apart, and a screen reader hears the author label on the message.
S8.42.where: Open menu > New chat > send any message > look at the author name for your message (You) and for the reply (the model name or AGI)

S8.43.note: The Step line only appears when both the completed and total step counts are known.
steps: Tap Open menu; if Agents is not listed, tap More first.
Tap Agents, then tap an agent whose status is running or waiting.
Look at the progress bar and the line that reads Step N of M, when both counts are known.
Compare with Expected: the bar fills as steps complete and the line changes.
For a spinner, open Projects while cloud projects are syncing and look for Loading projects.
S8.43.where: Open menu > Agents > tap an agent that is running > look at the bar and the Step N of M line under it

S8.44.needs: a signed-in account; a slow connection makes the placeholders easier to see
S8.44.note: The placeholders show only during the first load, so on a fast connection they may pass too quickly to see.
steps: Tap Open menu.
Tap More if Schedules is folded, then tap Schedules.
Look during the first load: three grey placeholder cards appear before the list.
Compare with Expected: the placeholders stand in for schedule cards and are replaced when the data arrives.
S8.44.where: Open menu > More > Schedules, while the list is loading for the first time

labels.text: Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats.

S8.45.note: Durations come from TOAST_DURATION_MS (5 seconds) and TOAST_ACTION_DURATION_MS (8 seconds) in apps/mobile/src/shared/components/Toast.tsx.
steps: Tap Open menu.
Long-press an AGI Cloud chat, then tap Archive.
Look for the bar that appears above the bottom edge with the archive message and an Undo button.
Wait and watch: it should leave by itself after about 5 seconds (about 8 seconds when it has a button).
Compare with Expected: it does not block the screen and it dismisses itself.
S8.45.where: Open menu > long-press a chat > Archive > look at the bar at the bottom: Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats. with Undo

S8.46.needs: a way to make sending fail, such as airplane mode
S8.46.note: The exact wording depends on the error, so the message after the colon varies.
steps: Tap Open menu, then the new-chat button (New chat).
Turn on airplane mode.
Type a message and send it.
Look at the alert above the message box; it has alert semantics and starts with Message failed to send:.
Compare with Expected: a clear error appears inline with the cause, and the reply can be retried from the banner.
S8.46.where: Open menu > New chat > turn on airplane mode > send a message > look at the alert above the message box: Message failed to send:

S8.47.needs: an account and a provider that triggers the consent strip
S8.47.note: The strip shows only when consent is missing, and the trigger was not traced end to end; a usage-limit banner is also rendered in the same screen.
steps: Tap Open menu, then the new-chat button (New chat).
Send a message to a provider whose use is not yet approved.
Look at the full-width strip above the message box; it has a globe icon, a message and a Review button.
Tap Review or the dismiss control to confirm they respond.
Compare with Expected: the strip sits in its own band, does not cover the chat, and can be dismissed.
S8.47.where: Open menu > New chat > send a message to a provider that needs consent > look at the strip above the message box with the Review button

S8.48.needs: an AGI Cloud account with more chats than one page
S8.48.note: The Library list loads more by scrolling and has no button, so it is not a pagination control.
steps: Tap Open menu.
Scroll to the bottom of the chat list.
Tap Load older chats and wait for the next page.
Compare with Expected: the next page of chats appears, and the button goes away when no older chats remain.
Optionally open Settings > Data Controls > Archived chats and tap Load more.
S8.48.where: Open menu > scroll to the bottom of the chat list > tap Load older chats (also Settings > Data Controls > Archived chats > Load more)

S8.49.needs: a paid account that can create schedules (a Free account sees the locked title instead)
S8.49.note: A Free account sees the title Scheduled tasks require Basic instead of No Schedules, with a View Plans button when purchases are available.
steps: Tap Open menu, then More if needed, then Schedules.
Look at the empty state: it shows the title No Schedules and a short description.
Look for the Try a template section and the Create Schedule button.
Compare with Expected: the message says what the view is for and gives a next step.
S8.49.where: Open menu > More > Schedules, with no schedules in the account

S8.50.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a network failure (airplane mode)
S8.50.note: The same pattern exists for projects: Retry loading projects appears on the Projects tab when syncing fails.
steps: Turn on airplane mode, then tap Open menu to open the chat list.
Look for the red error text and the Retry button in the list.
Turn off airplane mode, tap Retry, and check that the chats load.
Compare with Expected: the error sits in the list with a recovery button, and the list fills once Retry works.
S8.50.where: Open menu > (the chat list fails to load on an AGI Cloud account) > tap Retry under the error text
